label: Service criticality
hint: Use business impact and institutional tiers. High criticality strengthens recovery and assurance requirements; it does not automatically dictate placement.

options.low: Low — limited impact and workable alternative

label: Financial / systemic criticality
hint: Characterize the solution’s role in monetary, payment, settlement or financial-stability services. This strengthens mandatory impact and recovery checks; it is not a universal cloud prohibition.

label: Mandatory execution location
hint: Choose on-premises when an institutional requirement prohibits external execution. This directly excludes external cloud, SaaS and hybrid cloud components. Costs cannot override it.

options.local: Must remain on-premises — external cloud prohibited

label: Sovereignty constraint on external hosting
hint: Consider jurisdiction, identities, encryption keys, privileged access and control-plane authority, not only data residency. A conditional answer still requires supporting sovereignty evidence.

options.local: Institutional sovereignty requirement prohibits external hosting
options.conditional: External hosting may be considered if sovereignty controls are evidenced

label: Data classification
hint: Suggested labels only: map these to your institution’s approved policy. Select the highest classification processed by the solution. Sensitivity alone does not require on-premises placement.

options.confidential: Confidential — disclosure could cause material harm
options.restricted: Restricted / highly sensitive — critical or tightly controlled information
options.unknown: Not yet classified — confirm with data owner

label: Personal data
hint: Personal data is a separate attribute from confidentiality. Confirm with the data owner.

options.ordinary: Personal data — identifiers, contacts, employee information
options.sensitive: Special-category or highly sensitive personal data

label: Demand & scaling pattern
hint: This answer also populates the demand question in the solution assessment.

options.elastic: Variable peaks, bursts or rapid scaling

label: Usage / concurrency pattern
hint: Choose the relevant pattern, then record user counts or rates in the sizing details.

options.interactive: Interactive users — specify total and concurrent users
options.transaction: Transactions / APIs — specify requests or transactions per second
options.batch: Batch / scheduled jobs — specify volume and processing window
options.mixed: Mixed users, transactions and batch processing

label: Compute requirements
hint: Select the main compute characteristic. Add CPU, memory or processing-time estimates if known.

options.unknown: Vendor requirements or sizing not confirmed

label: Storage & data behavior
hint: Describe initial capacity, growth, retention and I/O or throughput targets in the details.

options.bulk: Large files, data sets or high-throughput processing
options.mixed: Mixed transactional and bulk / archive data

label: Hardware availability constraint
hint: A GPU or HSM does not automatically require local execution. Choose local only when institutional control or physical proximity makes it mandatory. This updates the hardware assessment question.

options.standard: Standard infrastructure or provider-supplied hardware is acceptable
options.local: Local physical / dedicated equipment is mandatory

label: Service operating window
hint: Availability hours are separate from recovery targets (RTO / RPO).

options.always: 24 hours a day, 7 days a week

label: Availability requirement
hint: Choose an architectural requirement; this is not a measured SLA. Record approved numerical targets in the details if available.

options.continuous: Continuous service; redundant design / failover required

label: Expected growth
hint: Use an estimate supported by the business. Specify annual percentages or forecast volumes where known.

label: id
hint: Use a unique reference for one workload or end-to-end service. Keep the same ID when comparing candidates.

label: name
hint: Name the capability being assessed, rather than a server or vendor product. Set a boundary that can be assessed as one service.

label: owner
hint: Who inside the institution is accountable for the service outcome and requirements? Identify a person or role, even when operation will be outsourced.

label: classificationNotes
hint: State the institutional classification label and describe the data types, handling limits or exceptions that apply.

label: capability
hint: Describe the outcome the workload must deliver: for whom, what it does, when it must be available, and what success means. Describe target needs for this design.

label: RTO — hours
hint: RTO = maximum acceptable time to restore the service after disruption. Enter the target in hours and explain the business deadline. Use decimal hours for shorter durations. This is a target, not an assumed provider promise.

label: RPO — minutes
hint: RPO = maximum acceptable loss of data, measured in time. Enter the target in minutes; this is a data-loss window, not restoration time. An RPO of 15 minutes means up to 15 minutes of recent changes may be lost. Zero requires an explicit no-data-loss requirement.

label: jurisdiction
hint: State approved or prohibited locations for data, backups, telemetry and support access. Include who controls encryption keys and administration. “EU hosting” alone does not settle jurisdiction or control sovereignty.

label: latency
hint: Identify which interactions need low delay or local proximity. Give a measured target where known, the endpoints, throughput and data-transfer volumes. If no tight constraint exists, say so.

label: dependencies
hint: List each service the workload needs, its owner, and what happens if it fails. Cover identity, keys, DNS, network links, data sources, integrations and providers. Include recovery order and telemetry/incident interfaces.

label: needs
hint: Describe baseline and peak demand, growth, storage, performance, operating hours and availability. Identify any HSM, GPU, dedicated hardware, container runtime, license or AI requirement. Separate confirmed needs from assumptions.

label: How is the software supplied?
hint: Use the product documentation. For a new solution, use the intended architecture. This identifies compatible service models only. Placement also requires confirmed location constraints, cloud permission and capacity or cost evidence.

options.modern: Custom solution compatible with managed runtimes
options.ai: Specialized AI workload — dedicated accelerator / model infrastructure

label: Must the solution execute on institution-controlled premises?
hint: Answer Yes only for an approved requirement covering execution or infrastructure control. Sensitive data alone does not automatically require local execution.

label: Can external cloud processing and administration be permitted?
hint: Consider data, backups, telemetry, jurisdiction, privileged access and encryption keys. This is institutional permission, not proof that a specific provider complies.

options.yes: Permitted, subject to provider and control validation

label: Does the service require components in both local and cloud environments?
hint: Choose Yes for an intentional split architecture. A cloud solution calling local identity alone does not necessarily require composite placement.

options.yes: Yes — intentional local and cloud components
options.no: No — a single execution environment is suitable

label: Is there a hard local proximity constraint?
hint: Examples include latency that remote execution cannot meet, very high local data volumes, or direct connection to local dedicated equipment. Record measurements in the solution profile.

options.hard: Yes — remote execution cannot satisfy it
options.flexible: No — engineered remote connectivity is feasible

label: Is local dedicated hardware required?
hint: Examples: a locally controlled HSM, physical licensing device or specialized appliance. An available cloud GPU is not a local-only requirement.

options.local: Yes — local physical / dedicated equipment is mandatory
options.standard: No — standard or provider-supplied infrastructure is suitable

label: Which hosting pattern is supported?
hint: Select a supported pattern, not an aspiration. Confirm vendor support, runtime compatibility and licensing before finalizing.

options.managed: Managed runtime / database / platform services supported
options.self: Institution controls OS / middleware / virtual machines
options.unknown: Not confirmed / not applicable to SaaS

label: What is the demand profile?
hint: Consider peaks, idle periods, expected growth and time to provision. Elastic demand is a reason to consider cloud, not permission to bypass controls.

options.elastic: Variable / burst demand; rapid scaling needed

label: What is the assessor’s lifecycle-economic conclusion?
hint: Record an assessor-supplied conclusion requiring supporting evidence. Compare equivalent service requirements over the same assessment period, including operations, connectivity, security, recovery and exit. The tool does not calculate TCO or establish economic superiority. Leave unconfirmed if no comparable estimates exist. Record the ability to fund purchases and recurring payments separately in Funding and procurement below.

options.cloud: Assessor conclusion — cloud favored; supporting evidence required
options.local: Assessor conclusion — local favored; supporting evidence required
options.similar: Assessor conclusion — comparable / no clear cost advantage

label: What is the solution’s service criticality?
hint: Use business impact and institutional tiers. High criticality strengthens recovery and assurance requirements; it does not automatically dictate placement.

options.low: Low — limited impact and workable alternative

label: Are recovery targets and dependencies defined?
hint: Define RTO (restoration time in hours), RPO (acceptable data-loss window in minutes), backup independence, trusted recovery and the recovery order of dependencies. A target is not evidence of a tested design.

options.yes: Targets and recovery dependencies are documented

label: How much direct institutional operational control is required?
hint: Separate accountable ownership from executing tasks. The institution retains accountability under every operating model.

options.retain: Institution must execute privileged / critical operations
options.shared: Institution and provider may divide operations

label: What internal operating capability is available?
hint: Consider coverage, skills, on-call capacity, platform lifecycle, incident handling and recovery—not only project implementation skills.

options.strong: Internal team can operate the full scope
options.partial: Internal capability covers part of the scope
options.limited: Limited internal capability for this scope

label: Is external operational sourcing permitted?
hint: Distinguish broad managed operations from bounded specialist support. Procurement permission does not establish supplier assurance.

label: Who needs network access to the solution?
hint: Describe the required exposure, not whether a firewall is already installed. Consider users, APIs, integrations and administrative interfaces. Internet access does not require cloud hosting; internal access does not establish security.

options.partners: Institutional networks and approved external partners
options.mixed: Mixed internal, partner and internet-facing access

label: What isolation does the hosting environment require?
hint: Record the required separation between workloads and administration. Dedicated infrastructure may exist locally or with a provider; validate the actual architecture rather than assuming that a location guarantees isolation.

options.baseline: Shared platform with standard access and network controls
options.segmented: Strong logical segmentation and separate administrative boundaries
options.dedicated: Dedicated physical resources / hardware isolation required

label: Who must control encryption keys and their lifecycle?
hint: Include generation, access, rotation, revocation and recovery. Institution-controlled keys do not by themselves remove provider jurisdiction or administrative exposure.

options.institution: Institution retains control of keys and lifecycle decisions
options.provider: Provider-managed keys may be accepted subject to institutional review
options.unknown: Key ownership and recovery responsibilities not yet defined

label: What recovery capability is required after a cyber compromise?
hint: Cyber recovery concerns trustworthy backups, identities, configurations and administration after compromise. Backup or replication alone does not demonstrate that capability. Specify the requirement; evidence is reviewed outside this questionnaire.

options.isolated: Isolated / immutable recovery sources with separate administration
options.rebuild: Rebuild from trusted configurations, identities and protected data sources
options.both: Isolated recovery sources and trusted rebuild capability
options.undefined: Only ordinary backup / DR is described; cyber recovery still needs definition

label: Does the solution require infrastructure for AI workloads?
hint: Identify training, inference, model / data volumes, accelerator needs, storage throughput and capacity utilization. AI can use servers, containers or managed services; a GPU alone does not select a location.

options.unknown: AI infrastructure needs not yet established

label: Does the software, platform or hardware contain embedded AI capabilities?
hint: Examples: built-in copilots, AI diagnostics in appliances, storage or network hardware, or vendor telemetry analysis. Consider enabled and planned capabilities, including calls to external models.

options.none: No enabled or planned embedded AI capability
options.yes: Embedded AI is enabled or planned

label: What authority will AI have over infrastructure operations?
hint: Select the highest intended authority. A0–A2 do not execute production changes. A3 requires approval before execution; A4 requires a predefined, explicitly approved operating boundary. This answer does not authorize AI actions.

options.none: No AI used for infrastructure operations
options.A0: A0 Observation — read and interpret authorized information
options.A1: A1 Assistance — diagnostics, correlation and summaries
options.A2: A2 Recommendation — propose actions for human decision
options.A3: A3 Approved Execution — execute specifically approved actions
options.A4: A4 Bounded Autonomy — act within explicitly approved limits

label: Where will AI process data, telemetry and operational context?
hint: This applies to AI workloads and enabled or planned embedded AI in software, platforms or hardware. Include prompts, logs, configuration, model APIs and support telemetry. Embedded AI may send context externally even without a training or inference workload.

options.none: Not applicable — no AI capability is used
options.local: AI processing remains within institutional premises
options.external: AI uses external models / APIs or transfers context externally
options.unknown: AI data flows or external dependencies not confirmed

label: Comparable lifecycle costs — evidence reference
hint: Identify the comparison, its owner and date. Cover equivalent service requirements, infrastructure / subscriptions, licensing, operations, connectivity, security, recovery and exit. A stated preference is an assessor-supplied conclusion; the tool does not calculate TCO.

label: Common economic assessment period
hint: State the same assessment horizon for each arrangement, for example five years, and identify included commitments.

label: Baseline demand
hint: Record measured or forecast volumes, utilization and normal capacity with units and the source.

label: Peak demand
hint: Record peak volumes, duration, frequency and response-time requirements with units and assumptions.

label: Scaling capability
hint: Explain supported scaling limits, provisioning time, quotas and platform / provider evidence.

label: Capacity assumptions
hint: Record headroom, growth, utilization, redundancy, recovery capacity and any accelerator assumptions.

label: Operating capability — scope and evidence
hint: Identify the required skills, staffing, support hours, on-call coverage, lifecycle and recovery responsibilities. Record evidence and gaps; this does not approve an operating model.

label: AI data and context flows — details
hint: When AI is relevant, identify capabilities, prompts, data, telemetry, APIs, processing locations, support access and external dependencies. A processing-location answer alone is not a complete data-flow record.

label: Can the required purchases and service payments be funded?
hint: Assess the proposed arrangement, including hardware, software, implementation and recurring services. Approval of funding is separate from architecture and deployment approval.

options.approved: Funding confirmed for the assessed scope and period
options.conditional: Funding is partial or depends on approval
options.unfunded: Required purchases or service payments cannot currently be funded
options.existing: Existing funded capacity and contracts cover the requirements

label: What must be purchased upfront, and what budget is available?
hint: List hardware / materials, software licences, installation, integration and migration. Record estimated cost and available capital budget, currency, funding source, budget owner, approval status and any shortfall. Leave unknown amounts unconfirmed.

label: Can the recurring service and operating costs be sustained?
hint: Include subscriptions, cloud consumption, support, managed services, staffing, connectivity, energy, recovery and renewals. Record recurring budget, assessment period, cost growth, committed minimum spend, payment terms and funding gaps.

label: What could delay or prevent buying the required materials and services?
hint: Record purchasing approvals, tender / contracting lead times, supplier availability, delivery dates, licence and contract restrictions, payment or foreign-currency exposure and the required service start date. Distinguish confirmed blockers from unverified risks.

label: How will funding or procurement gaps be resolved, and by whom?
hint: Record the Finance / procurement owner, evidence references, approvals needed and target dates. Consider reuse, phased acquisition or a funded service arrangement only if mandatory requirements and sustainable recurring costs are satisfied. This plan is not purchase approval.

label: Is a feasible exit from the cloud provider available?
hint: Required for external cloud, SaaS and the cloud components of a hybrid service. The institution must be able to retrieve all required information and restore, migrate or replace the service in another supported environment. A backup inside the same provider, or a promise that data can be exported, is insufficient on its own.

options.tested: Feasible exit documented and demonstrated in a test
options.documented: Feasible exit documented; demonstration / test still required
options.blocked: No feasible exit — data or service cannot be recovered or migrated
options.unknown: Exit feasibility has not been confirmed

label: How will all required data and configuration be retrieved?
hint: List business data, attachments, metadata, logs / records, schemas, configuration and the keys or documented access needed to use them. Record complete export or replication formats, ownership / contractual access rights, checks for completeness and integrity, and independent access if the provider becomes unavailable. Do not enter actual keys or credentials.

label: How will the service be restored, migrated or replaced outside this provider?
hint: Describe portable backups and a restore procedure, full data export and rebuild, replication, or another supported migration / replacement method. Explain encryption-key availability, software / licence and dependency compatibility, and how the data will be usable at the destination. Record test evidence, results or a planned demonstration; same-provider restore alone does not demonstrate exit.

label: Where can the service and data run after exit, and within what time?
hint: Identify an on-premises or alternative-provider destination, capacity, software support, operating owner, jurisdiction and security controls. Record achievable recovery / migration time, data-loss tolerance, dependency recovery order, cutover, reconciliation and rollback. The destination must satisfy the solution requirements.

label: What are the exit costs, contractual conditions and responsible owners?
hint: Record export / egress charges, transition funding, notice periods, termination rights, provider assistance, access during transition, secure deletion / retention obligations and removal of provider access. Identify service, infrastructure and procurement owners, the exit trigger, plan / contract references, last review and next test date.

label: rationale
hint: Explain why the proposed placement and operating arrangement fit the solution, and identify assumptions or alternatives that still need review.

label: conditions
hint: List the conditions to resolve and the evidence that must be reviewed before the final decision.

label: owner
hint: Identify the institutional person or role accountable for the decision.

label: platform
hint: Identify who owns the hosting platform and its technical standards.

label: operator
hint: Identify who will run the solution and the agreed operational scope.

label: authority
hint: Identify the institutional authority responsible for final approval. Recording a name does not grant approval.

label: review
hint: State when the decision must be reviewed, or which change should trigger reassessment.
